strongElements.quote: I think potentially the, um, the units sold

after.topFix: Practice sizing the fix out loud from the P&L: write the equation first, compute, then sanity-check. Here, costs were 94% of revenue (58 + 22 + 14). A 10% price rise gives 94/110 ≈ 85.5% costs, or about a 14.5% margin. Restoring 24% needs 94/0.76 ≈ 1.237, about a 24% price increase. Your claims of "ten percent" and then "about fifty percent" both fail that check, and that is what turned a sound pricing recommendation into one you couldn't defend.
